info.bio: Jamie "Robbie" Robertson es un vocalista y guitarrista canadiense. Originario de un padre judío y de madre Mohawk Desde pequeño, aprendió a tocar la guitarra en una escuela de Toronto y comenzó a escribir sus propias canciones cuando tenía 10 años. Fue el líder de The Band, un grupo de música canadiense que inició en 1967 y se retiró en 1976. Después, el grupo musical, ya sin Robertson, volvió al mundo de la música en 1983, se retiraron en 1999.

scenes.name: Los autores (1975-1990)
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La emancipación definitiva de la mujer en el rock (Terry Garthwaite, Joan Armatrading, Nanci Griffith y, sobre todo, Rickie Lee Jones, protegida de Tom Waits); la escuela tejana de cantautores herederos de Townes Van Zandt (Guy Clark, Butch Hancock, Joe Ely, Terry Allen, Rodney Crowell, T-Bone Burnett); el populismo melancólico de la posguerra de Vietnam (Warren Zevon, Rick Danko, Steve Forbert, John Hiatt, John Mellencamp, Don Henley, Donald Fagen, Robbie Robertson); y el puente de 1977 hacia la new wave: Peter Gabriel, poeta atormentado de las neurosis postindustriales, Marianne Faithfull y Kate Bush.

podcast.title: Childhood and Adoption
podcast.body: Robbie's biological father was tragically killed while changing a flat tire on the side of a highway. He was subsequently adopted by his mother's second husband, and although they lived in Toronto, his mother frequently traveled back to Six Nations to visit family, maintaining his connection to his heritage. "Robbie's biological father was killed while changing a flat tire on the side of a highway. He was adopted by his mother's second husband and then they lived at a Toronto but mom frequently traveled back to Six Nations to visit family."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Musical Influences
podcast.body: As a child, Robbie had a radio through which he listened to rock and blues music broadcast from American stations, laying the foundation for his future musical career. He also worked as a carny, including in a freak show, before he started playing in bands at the age of 14. "Robbie had a radio on which he listened to rock and blues coming in from American stations. He worked as a carny as a kid, including in a freak show, before he started playing in band at the age of 14."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Film Music Contributions
podcast.body: Robbie Robertson extensively worked on music for several films directed by Martin Scorsese, including *Casino*, *Gangs of New York*, and *The Wolf of Wall Street*. He also collaborated on film work with director Oliver Stone. "It's also worth noting that Robbie worked on the music for The Martin Scorsese movie Casino and Gangs of New York and The Wolf of Wall Street and a couple of others. And he's also done film work with Oliver Stone too."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Kayuga and Mohawk Heritage
podcast.body: Robbie Robertson's mother was Kayuga and Mohawk, and she raised him on the Six Nations Reserve located west of Toronto. This strong connection to his Indigenous roots deeply influenced his later work. "His mom was a Kayuga and Mohawk raised on the Six Nations Reserve west of Toronto."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Numerous Accolades
podcast.body: Robbie Robertson has been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, Canada's Walk of Fame, and the Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame. He is also an Officer of the Order of Canada and a recipient of the Governor-General's Performing Arts Award, and inspired the Aboriginal Lifetime Achievement Award. "He's in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. He's in Canada's Waka fame. He has a Governor-General's Performing Arts Award. He's in the Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame. He's also an Officer of the Order of Canada and he inspired the Aboriginal Lifetime Achievement Award."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Band's Canadian Makeup
podcast.body: One of the most "American sounding rock groups of the 20th century," The Band, was fascinatingly made up of Robbie Robertson and a bunch of other Canadians, with the sole exception of drummer Levon Helm, who was from Arkansas. "And it's fascinating that one of the most American sounding rock groups of the 20th century was actually made up of Robbie and a bunch of other Canadians. The only non-Canadian was drummer Lee von Helme, he was Mark and Saw."

xref.title: Robbie Robertson Death (August 9, 2023) – Prostate Cancer, Age 80; Musical Collaborator with Martin Scorsese
xref.body: Robbie Robertson was the guitarist, musical director, and chief songwriter of the Band — a Canadian group widely credited with helping create the genre of Americana. He was also a frequent and celebrated musical collaborator with director Martin Scorsese on several of his best-known films. He died of prostate cancer on August 9, 2023, age 80. "It's interesting how a Canadian band helped create a whole new genre of music called Americana."
